summary: Grant Parker is a historian and Indologist who earned an MA from the University of Cape Town (1989–1991) and a PhD from Princeton University (1993–1999). He taught at Duke University (1999–2006) and joined Stanford University in 2006.

Graves Champney Haughton (1788–1849) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Fort William College (1812, ~1813–1815). He taught at East India Company College (1817–1827), founded the Royal Asiatic Society, and served as its secretary (~1831–1832).

Gray Tuttle is a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history. He studied at Princeton (BA) and Harvard (MA), supervised by Nicola Di Cosmo, William C. Kirby, Leonard van der Kuijp, and Philip A. Kuhn, before joining Columbia University in 2005.

Graziadio Isaia Ascoli (1829–1907) was an Italian linguist and Indologist who studied under tutor Samuel David Luzzatto. He served as a professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1861 to 1902 and founded the Archivio Glottologico Italiano in 1873.

Greg Bailey is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Melbourne under J. Durham in 1980 and studied under Madeleine Biardeau. He was a visiting research fellow at Tübingen (1998) and held posts at La Trobe University.

Gregor Ahn is a scholar of religious and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Bonn (under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit) and Copenhagen, held posts at Münster and Tartu, and has been a professor of comparative religion at Heidelberg University since 1996.

Gregorio Franzò (b. 1879) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Pisa and the Scuola Normale Superiore from 1901 to 1904, later teaching "materie letterarie" as a professor at Liceo Classico Carducci Ricasoli.

Gregory Adam Scott works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and holds posts attested in 2026 at the University of Edinburgh and at the University of Manchester as Senior Lecturer in Chinese Culture and History.

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher, studied under Birgit Kellner and several traditional teachers, and undertook doctoral studies supervised by Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Gregory Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Virginia in 1993, held an attested post there in 2002, and is a continuing lecturer at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

Gregory L. Possehl (1941–2011) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Walter A. Fairservis, Jr. and served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (attested in 2006).

Gregory Max Seton specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned degrees from Naropa, UC Santa Barbara, and Oxford (D.Phil 2015), studying under Alexis Sanderson, Vesna Wallace, Harunaga Isaacson, Lance S. Cousins, and several Tibetan masters.

Gregory Nagy is a linguist who completed his undergraduate studies at Indiana University Bloomington (~1958–1962) and his graduate studies at Harvard University (~1962–1966), where he held a post in 2025.

Gregory P. A. Levine is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history. Educated at Oberlin College and Princeton University, he became an Associate Professor of Japanese art, architecture, and Buddhist visual cultures at UC Berkeley around 2003.

Gregory Price Grieve is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. Educated at San Francisco State and the University of Chicago, he taught at Chicago and DePaul before becoming Professor and Head of Religious Studies at UNC Greensboro in 2002.

Gregory Schopen is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at ANU under J.W. de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana. He held faculty posts at Indiana, UT Austin, Brown, Stanford, and UCLA as Distinguished Professor Emeritus.

Grigorij Fedorovich Ilyin (1914–1985) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Moscow State University under Peter Peterson and Igor Reisner, he held posts at the Diplomatic Academy (1947–1953), the USSR Academy of Sciences (1952), and the University of Chicago (1953).

Grigorij Lukich Nakhutsrishvili (1922–1984) was an Indologist, linguist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tbilisi State University (~1944–1949), where he began teaching in 1952 and became chair in 1976.

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin (1933–2008) was a historian, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Moscow State University and under George de Roerich, he held posts at the Institute of Oriental Studies, Moscow State University, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Gritli von Mitterwallner (1925–2012) was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist. She completed her Dr. phil. (~1958–1964) and Habilitation (~1964–1971) at the University of Munich, where she served as a professor from 1978 to 1991.
